summary: Defensive, low-abuse product with no customer-data custody, so legal exposure is modest. The real issues are the 'malware cannot reach the other side' warranty, employer privacy duties over an 'unrestricted' personal-use OS, broker-dealer recordkeeping for traders using an unmonitored side, and OS licensing for a second Windows instance. All are fixable with contracts, policy controls and careful claims.

objections.objection: The MVP promises 'malware in one OS cannot reach the other'. Hypervisor escapes and side-channel flaws exist; a bank breached through the product will point at that claim. Absolute isolation claims create warranty, misrepresentation and regulator-scrutiny exposure; contracts must cap liability and marketing must avoid guarantees.

Traders and finance staff get an unrestricted OS. Broker-dealers must retain all business communications; staff using personal messaging or webmail on the open side recreates the off-channel communications problem regulators fine banks for. The product must keep business communications on the captured side or it hands target customers a compliance gap.

Central management of both OS images means the employer controls and can inspect an environment marketed for personal freedom. In the EU, workplace monitoring falls under GDPR and national employee-data rules (works councils); the product needs clear separation of what is logged on the open side, transparency material and a DPIA template.

Running a second Windows instance in a VM needs appropriate virtualization licensing rights (e.g. Enterprise/VDA-style rights); customers may face extra OS licence cost, and OS-vendor terms limit what a third-party hypervisor can ship. Pricing that claims savings versus a second laptop must account for this.

A thin hypervisor beneath Windows is architecturally what hyperjacking rootkits do; a compromised update channel would give an attacker total control of privileged endpoints. Needs signed updates, secure-boot integration and a disclosure/patch policy to meet customer vendor-risk and regulator outsourcing expectations.

strongest_point: Purely defensive tool that holds no customer data, credentials or PII off-device, so dual-use and data-custody risk is low compared with most security products.
what_would_change_my_mind: Customer contract template with capped liability and no absolute isolation guarantee, reviewed by counsel at two pilot banks.
Design where communications tools run only on the corporate side and the open side blocks business email/messaging domains, accepted by a broker-dealer compliance officer.
Written OS-licensing position (from the OS vendor or licensing counsel) showing the second instance is covered by licences customers already own.
